prompt: We are a European e-commerce retailer opening a Saudi entity and an online store for Saudi customers. No government contracts. What Saudi regulations apply to us, and what should our first 90 days of compliance work look like?
assertions: Delivers an applicability determination BEFORE detail: Saudi PDPL applies (personal data of Saudi residents); NCA ECC-2:2024 is NOT mandatory for a private non-CNI retailer (recommended best practice only); SAMA and CST licensing regimes do not apply to a plain retailer — each conclusion tied to the right regulator (SDAIA / NCA / SAMA / CST)
States the PDPL enforcement reality: Royal Decree M/19 as amended by M/148, fully enforced since September 14, 2024, with SDAIA actively enforcing (first-wave violation decisions issued in 2025-26)

Names concrete PDPL first-90-days actions: controller registration on SDAIA's National Data Governance Platform, RoPA, lawful bases (including the M/148 legitimate-interest basis for non-sensitive data), privacy notices, and a transfer mechanism for EU-KSA data flows (SDAIA SCC modules / adequacy / BCRs)
States the breach-notification rule correctly: 72 hours to SDAIA (via the platform), with data-subject notification where they are at risk

States penalty exposure correctly: fines up to SAR 5M per violation (doubling for repeat), with criminal exposure for unlawful disclosure of sensitive data — without inventing enacted amendments (the 2025 graduated-penalty proposals are not enacted as of August 2026; a compliant answer either omits them or flags them as pending)
